s: Deduplicate first, at the lowest grain, so nothing downstream is multiplied.
Filter on the order header (status, customer, date) after joining lines to orders.
Round each line to cents in its own currency, convert with the order month's rate, round again: the same convention Finance uses.
Group by the region name; check that the five rows add up to the total.

code.title: Q1 2026 gross sales by selling region (portable SQL)
src: SELECT DISTINCT * FROM order_lines             -- the March re-export duplicated some rows
JOIN orders AS o ON o.OrderID = l.OrderID
JOIN regions AS r ON r.RegionKey = q1.SalesRegionKey

s: Count orders with COUNT(DISTINCT OrderID): after the join there is one row per line.
Count lines with COUNT(*) on the deduplicated lines.
Customers: COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID). The channel rows will add up to more than the total, because some customers buy in several channels.

code.title: Totals with correct counts
src: WITH lines AS (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM order_lines),
JOIN orders AS o ON o.OrderID = l.OrderID
-- COUNT(*) here would count lines, not orders

s: Start from the table whose rows you must keep: customers.
Put every condition on the right-hand tables (status, dates, test customer) in the ON clauses, not in WHERE.
Use COALESCE(SUM(...), 0) so customers without sales show 0, not NULL.

code.title: All customers with their Q1 2026 sales
src: WITH lines AS (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM order_lines),
SUM(ROUND(ROUND(l.Qty * l.UnitPrice * (100 - l.DiscountPct) / 100.0, 2) * COALESCE(fx.USDPerUnit, 1), 2)) AS GrossUSD
JOIN lines AS l ON l.OrderID = o.OrderID
LEFT JOIN fx_rates AS fx ON fx.Month = SUBSTRING(CAST(o.OrderDate AS VARCHAR(10)), 1, 7) AND fx.Currency = o.Currency
WHERE o.Status = 'Completed' AND o.OrderDate >= '2026-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2026-04-01'
SUM(CASE WHEN s.CustomerID IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS WithoutQ1Sales
LEFT JOIN sales AS s ON s.CustomerID = c.CustomerID   -- filters live inside the CTE, not in WHERE
